products.name: XBOW Platform
products.description: Autonomous offensive security / AI penetration testing platform that continuously discovers, chains, and validates real exploits against web applications (per xbow.com and third-party coverage).

products.name: XBOW Pentest On-Demand
products.description: Announced Nov 2025 — a self-serve, fixed-price autonomous pentest product delivering an audit-ready report within days (Lightspeed Plus $4,000 / Lightspeed Premium $8,000 / Enterprise custom quote, per Penetrify.cloud pricing analysis and BusinessWire).

features.name: Autonomous exploit chaining
features.description: Chains multiple vulnerabilities into real, working attack paths rather than flagging isolated findings.
features.how_it_works: Uses AI agents (reportedly built by former GitHub Copilot engineers) to reason about application context and attempt real exploitation end-to-end; validated on the public XBOW Benchmark of 104 containerized CTF-style web challenges across 26 vulnerability categories (arXiv papers, emergentmind.com).

features.name: Continuous / always-on testing
features.description: Runs nonstop rather than as a point-in-time engagement, retesting whenever the target application changes (Help Net Security, xbow.com via GeekWire).

features.name: Real exploit validation
features.description: Every finding is claimed to be a reproducible, working exploit rather than a theoretical/scanner-style flag (xbow.com messaging, corroborated by SecurityWeek/BusinessWire coverage).

features.name: Human-in-the-loop training/review
features.description: Team of experienced human hackers (assembled by CISO Nico Waisman) trains and reportedly reviews the autonomous system's output; critics note humans review reports before HackerOne submission (Rawsec blog, utkusen.substack.com).

pricing: Not fully published by XBOW as of enterprise platform pricing. For the 'Pentest On-Demand' product (launched Nov 2025), third-party pricing trackers report: Lightspeed Plus ~$4,000/test (lightweight apps), Lightspeed Premium ~$8,000/test (complex apps), Enterprise = custom quote; one competitor comparison (Escape.tech) states XBOW 'starts at $6,000 per pentest' with credit-pack enterprise pricing — figures vary by source and should be treated as approximate/unverified.
customers: Seznam (named in Series C extension coverage)

unverified: '100+ customers worldwide' claimed by company, including 'some of the most security-forward companies' and 'Fortune 500 companies' per SecurityWeek/GeekWire — most customer names not disclosed

research_highlights.title: How XBOW Ranked #1 in Autonomous Penetration Testing (company blog)
research_highlights.summary: Company's own account of reaching #1 on HackerOne's US leaderboard (primary source; included for context, not an outside claim).

research_highlights.title: Baselines Before Architecture: Evaluating Coding Agents for Autonomous Penetration Testing
research_highlights.summary: Independent academic evaluation of coding agents (e.g., Codex CLI/GPT-5) against the XBOW benchmark; found strong plain-agent baselines solve 70-81/104 tasks.

research_highlights.title: Multi-Agent Penetration Testing AI for the Web (MAPTA)
research_highlights.summary: Third-party multi-agent system achieving 76.9% success on the 104-task XBOW benchmark, with perfect scores on SSRF/misconfiguration categories.

research_highlights.title: AWE: Adaptive Agents for Dynamic Web Penetration Testing
research_highlights.summary: Third-party adaptive-agent system also evaluated against the XBOW benchmark suite.

research_highlights.title: Dead.Letter — How XBOW found an unauthenticated RCE on Exim (CVE-2026-45185)
research_highlights.summary: XBOW researcher (@fede_k) disclosure thread on a critical Exim mail server RCE credited to XBOW.

research_highlights.title: XBOW credited with critical Microsoft RCE, CVSS 9.8 (CVE-2026-21536)
research_highlights.summary: Critical RCE in Microsoft Devices Pricing Program credited to XBOW in March 2026 Patch Tuesday; two related Bing RCEs (CVE-2026-32194, CVE-2026-32191) also credited.

research_highlights.title: Does 'XBOW AI Hacker' Deserve the Hype?
research_highlights.summary: Independent security researcher critique arguing XBOW's HackerOne ranking is reputation-driven and its highest bounty (at time of writing) was only $3,000.

research_highlights.title: About the hype around XBOW
research_highlights.summary: Rawsec blog analysis questioning whether XBOW's automated findings represent genuinely novel/hard vulnerability classes versus already-known bug types.
